bib.title: A Broad-Coverage Challenge Corpus for Sentence Understanding through Inference

question: Can a multi-genre NLI corpus, collected like SNLI but from ten genres of written and spoken English, give a harder and broader benchmark for sentence understanding and cross-genre transfer?
hypothesis: SNLI's single image-caption genre limits coverage and leaves little headroom; a multi-genre corpus with comparable annotation quality should be substantially harder.
contributions: MultiNLI, 433k premise-hypothesis pairs from ten genres of written and spoken English
Matched/mismatched dev and test sets for explicit cross-genre evaluation
Baseline results with CBOW, BiLSTM and ESIM, and annotation-tag analysis of 13 linguistic phenomena

method.summary: Crowdworkers read a premise sentence from one of ten genres and write three hypotheses (entailment, neutral, contradiction); dev and test pairs are relabeled by four more workers and gold is the majority of five labels. Three sentence-pair models (CBOW, BiLSTM, ESIM) are trained on SNLI, MultiNLI, or a mix and tested on matched and mismatched genres.
method.task: natural language inference (3-way: entailment, neutral, contradiction)

datasets.name: MultiNLI
datasets.size: 392,702 train, 20,000 dev, 20,000 test (433k pairs total per abstract)
datasets.split: Train: 5 genres (FICTION, GOVERNMENT, SLATE, TELEPHONE, TRAVEL). Dev/test: 2,000 random examples per genre across all 10 genres; first 5 are matched, other 5 (9/11, FACE-TO-FACE, LETTERS, OUP, VERBATIM) mismatched. No premise in more than one set.
datasets.source: 9 genres from OANC 2nd release (downloaded 12/2016) plus FICTION compiled from freely available works; OANC permissive licence, FICTION under CC-SA/CC-BY/public domain. 387 annotators via Hybrid (gethybrid.io).
datasets.preprocessing: Unique sentences within genres, exclude premises under eight characters, manually remove non-narrative text (formulae, bibliographic references, lists).

datasets.name: SNLI
datasets.split: Standard; in mixed setting 15% random sample of SNLI train used (resampled each epoch)

models.name: CBOW
models.architecture: sentence = sum of word embeddings; concat of premise, hypothesis, difference, element-wise product -> single tanh layer -> 3-way softmax

models.name: BiLSTM
models.architecture: average of bidirectional LSTM states over words; same classifier as CBOW

models.name: ESIM
models.architecture: Enhanced Sequential Inference Model (Chen et al. 2017), base without TreeLSTM ensemble

training.dropout: ESIM 0.5; CBOW and BiLSTM 0.1 (tuned on SNLI dev); per-genre CBOW 0.2

other.mixed_setting: full MultiNLI train + random 15% of SNLI train each epoch

metrics.name: accuracy
metrics.definition: test-set accuracy of 3-way label vs gold label; examples without 3-vote consensus (gold '-') excluded

metrics.name: inter-annotator agreement
metrics.definition: percent of individual labels matching gold label in validated examples

eval.protocol: Matched and mismatched test; no seeds, repeats or significance tests stated. Dev tag analysis in Table 5.

prompts.purpose: Annotator instruction for written non-fiction genres (truncated)
prompts.text: This task will involve reading a line from a non-ﬁction article and writing three sentences that relate to it. The line will describe a situation or event. Using only this description and what you know about the world: Write one sentence that is deﬁnitely correct about the situation or event in the line. Write one sentence that might be correct about the situation or event in the line. Write one sentence that is deﬁnitely incorrect about the situation or event in the line.

limits: Baselines are only CBOW, BiLSTM and ESIM; no seeds, variance or significance tests stated; learning rate, batch size, epochs not given.
Models perform similarly on matched and mismatched sets, so the cross-genre transfer test is not yet discriminating; authors expect genre mismatch to matter as models improve.
Gold labels depend on annotator coreference assumptions; spurious cues (e.g. negation predicts contradiction) acknowledged; no hypothesis-only baseline.
Premises are single sentences; hypotheses written by crowdworkers (387, demographics unavailable). Dated: baselines far below later pretrained models.
